title: Transfer boundaries in affective audio modelling: analysis code, run records and manuscript

creators.name: Zhang, Jingyi
creators.affiliation: Shanghai Huangan Technology Co., Ltd., Shanghai, China; Systems Neuroscience, Institute for Neuroscience, D-HEST, ETH Zurich, Switzerland

creators.name: Yao, Xiaotong
creators.affiliation: Shanghai Huangan Technology Co., Ltd., Shanghai, China

description:
Analysis code, run records, figure sources and manuscript for a multi-corpus study of how far a mapping from acoustic descriptors to human affective response survives four changes of setting — new material, edited audio, a sensor in place of a self-report, and an individual listener — and of what each adaptation route tested recovers when it does not.

This archive supersedes an earlier preprint (arXiv:2608.27674), whose organising claim — that generalisation failures divide into two kinds with mutually exclusive remedies — is contradicted by this project's own measurements and is withdrawn. reports/TAC_revision_audit.md records what was withdrawn, corrected and recomputed, and what remains a stated limitation.

Two findings concern corpora in wide use and are useful independently of the main result. In Emo-Soundscapes, 613 of 1,213 clips are mixtures of thirty source recordings, and the distributed metadata gives every clip its own group identifier, so grouped cross-validation on the supplied groups provides no protection against near-duplicates spanning folds. In PMEmo, a sham using presentation position alone reproduces 114–249% of the stimulus-level reliability of its song-level electrodermal measures.

Licensing. Code is MIT (see LICENSE); manuscript text and figures are CC BY 4.0. The nine analysed corpora are third-party and are not redistributed here — several carry non-commercial terms and one has no audio redistribution right at all. Per-corpus terms, including whether derived files may be redistributed, are in DATA_LICENSES.md; read it before reusing anything built from them.

Reproducibility, stated plainly. The run records fix the script, the seed, the parameters and the resulting metrics. They do not pin the code: records were written from working trees with uncommitted changes, input hashes cover a minority of runs and output hashes are absent. The analyses reproduce from the scripts at the recorded parameters; they do not yet reproduce bit-for-bit from a pinned commit.
